title: Route strong and fast models
goal: Configure Claude Code and Codex so planning and review use the strong model and implementation uses the fast one, then record timings for one small task.

starter_prompts.claude: Read AGENTS.md and tests/routing.test.mjs. Fix the Claude Code routing config so plan mode uses Opus and execution uses Sonnet: set the default model in .claude/settings.json, make the reviewer subagent Opus and read-only, and make the implementer subagent Sonnet. Do not edit anything under tests/. Run npm test and show me the failures that remain (the Codex profiles and timings.md are next).
starter_prompts.codex: Read AGENTS.md and tests/routing.test.mjs. Fix the Codex side of the routing config: codex/fm-plan.config.toml (strong model, high effort, read-only sandbox), codex/fm-impl.config.toml (fast model, low effort, workspace-write) and .codex/agents/reviewer.toml (strong model, high effort, read-only). Use models that /model lists. Do not edit anything under tests/. Run npm test and report what still fails.

solution_notes: opusplan is one setting that switches between Opus (plan mode) and Sonnet (execution) for you. Codex has no single alias for this, so the plan and implement profiles are separate files you select per session with --profile.
The reviewer is read-only in both tools. Review that can edit code quietly turns into a second implementer, so the tool allowlist (Claude) and sandbox_mode (Codex) enforce the role.
Effort is the second dial. The Codex implementation profile drops to low effort on the fast model, and the plan and review roles keep high.
The timing table is the point: the fast model finishes implementation quickly, and the strong model's time is spent where a wrong decision is expensive to catch later.
